ideas.headline: Stable AI Prompt Variance Baselines for Brands
ideas.short_description: Measure repeated AI-answer variance across canonical brand prompts, then trace unstable claims to conflicting or missing public entity facts.
ideas.description: A brand creates a canonical prompt set such as “who owns X,” “what does X do,” and “when was X founded,” with optional market, language, and competitor variants. The service runs each prompt N times across configured AI models and, where available, separate accounts or locations; users can also upload manually captured outputs when a context cannot be automated. For every prompt, the dashboard reports citation-set Jaccard overlap, source-set churn, claim-level drift, answer agreement, and sample size, clearly separating observed variance from true change. Clicking an unstable prompt opens a diagnostic layer that compares the disputed claims against Wikidata, SEC EDGAR where relevant, and the brand’s Schema.org and sameAs markup, identifying conflicting, missing, stale, or ambiguous entity facts. The resulting report provides a baseline confidence score, raw run evidence, reproducible sampling settings, and prioritized corrections rather than pretending that one model response is a stable ranking.
ideas.value_proposition: Measure whether an AI visibility change is real before acting, then trace unstable prompt claims to the public entity facts that may be causing the drift.

ideas.headline: Make Every Important Answer Recoverable
ideas.short_description: The tool replays how a page’s answer gets lost, then proves the smallest structural fix that makes it recoverable.
ideas.description: The tool treats an important URL as a recoverable answer rather than a page to score. It reconstructs the shortest evidence path from a natural-language question to the page’s answer across raw HTML, rendered browser output, and public sitemap context. It then performs counterfactual removals of navigation, boilerplate, delayed scripts, and fragmented sections to identify exactly where answer recovery breaks. For each failure, the tool produces a concrete patch and a replayable receipt, allowing teams to verify that a page’s answer survives real extraction conditions over time.
ideas.value_proposition: Turn unstable AI visibility into a testable engineering problem: show the exact journey by which an answer disappears, identify the smallest structural repair, and continuously prove that the repair remains recoverable using only publicly obtainable page data.

Run deterministic perturbation tests that remove or delay scripts, hide navigation and boilerplate, collapse fragmented sections, and compare raw versus rendered states. Emit a failure receipt containing the URL, response/render state, selectors, text spans, and rule that caused answer loss. ideas.headline: Diagnose Why AI Search Omits Your Brand
ideas.short_description: Compare competitor mentions with crawl evidence to label each AI omission a citation gap or sampling noise—and prescribe the missing source action.
ideas.description: A team enters its brand, competitors, category, locations, and a set of decision prompts such as “best providers in [category]” or “which products compare well for [use case].” The product runs repeated, versioned responses through customer-authorized AI-search or model providers, identifies contexts where competitors are recommended but the brand is absent, and creates a matched claim record for each omission. It then searches Common Crawl’s published indexes and permitted WARC captures for third-party pages that mention the brand alongside the same category, use case, location, product attributes, or comparison language. When relevant crawl evidence exists but repeated model runs continue omitting the brand, the verdict is “likely sampling noise,” with rerun guidance; when relevant evidence is absent, the verdict is “citation gap,” listing the missing source types and contexts—such as independent comparison pages, local publications, product reviews, or location-specific service pages. Users receive an evidence-linked action queue, before-and-after rerun results, crawl-vintage labels, and exportable reports for PR, SEO, and content teams.
ideas.value_proposition: Give brand reputation teams a prompt-level verdict that explains whether an AI recommendation omission is caused by missing third-party evidence or model sampling noise, with an actionable source-building brief.

ideas.description: A London plumber or electrician installs the WordPress plugin and connects the service pages, approved price fields, service areas, and turnaround details already in the site.
